name: Marshall Jefferson
hook: Heard house music at the Music Box, decided it needed a piano, and wrote the genre's first real anthem.
blurb: Jefferson heard Ron Hardy's DJ sets at the Music Box in 1983 and started making his own tracks. "Move Your Body", also released as "The House Music Anthem", went round on cassette among Chicago dancers for a year before Trax would press it, and Ron Hardy, who had been playing it off reel-to-reel tape, mixed the released version himself in 1986. It is one of the clearest cases in Chicago house of a DJ's live reaction driving what got recorded. It was one of the first house records to use a piano, and that piano hook became a signature of the genre almost overnight. Its popularity outside Chicago helped house travel.

signatureTracks.title: Move Your Body (The House Music Anthem)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The piano chord that opens the track is often cited as the moment house music got its own instrumental signature, distinct from the disco and electro it grew out of.

signatureTracks.title: That's the Way Love Is (Ten City)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Jefferson produced Ten City's first two albums. This single went to number 1 on the US dance chart and number 8 in the UK: his deep house production behind Byron Stingily's soul vocal.
